_about: Every number the simulation and the cost model use. status: published = taken from the source; calibrated = tuned so the usual-care run matches the published figure (see scripts/calibrate.py); design = a choice of this system, not a fact; assumption = no published value found, kept and tested in the sensitivity analysis. Checked 11 Nov 2026.

usd_to_aed.source: Central Bank of the UAE: dirham pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725

whatsapp_per_message_usd.source: Meta WhatsApp Business Platform rate card, UAE, utility template (as reproduced by SleekFlow, Oct 2026)

sms_per_message_usd.source: Twilio outbound SMS price to the UAE (textbee.dev summary of Twilio's price page, checked Sep 2026)

hosting_per_hour_usd.source: Azure Standard_D4s_v5 on-demand price, UAE North region (devzero.io price table)

nurse_salary_per_year_aed.source: Payscale: median base salary of a registered nurse in the UAE

diabetes_cost_per_person_year_usd.source: IDF Diabetes Atlas 10th edition (2021): health spending per person with diabetes, UAE (via Statista)

outreach_nurses_new.source: Staffing plan of this system: two nurses run the outreach queue, staff calls and health-worker visits

outreach_nurses_usual_care.source: Usual care: one nurse handles reminder lists

primary_care_visit_aed.source: Typical GP consultation in Abu Dhabi, AED 220 (indicative range 120-450), Zavis UAE price directory. An aggregator estimate, not the DoH Mandatory Tariff; used for every attended visit in both ways; no separate published price was found for a telehealth or mobile-clinic visit, so the same price is used (the range is shown as well)

primary_care_visit_aed_range.source: Indicative range of a GP consultation in Abu Dhabi, AED 120 to 450 (Zavis UAE price directory); used to show how much the cost per person depends on the visit price

reply_whatsapp.source: Fabens et al. 2024, JMIR Formative Research: 23% of WhatsApp users replied to two-way follow-up messages

reply_sms.source: Fabens et al. 2024, JMIR Formative Research: 20% of SMS users replied

phone_vs_sms_ratio.source: Study within a trial (2019): attendance 23% after a phone reminder vs 18% after SMS (23/18)

home_visit_reply.source: No published reply rate for a health-worker home visit; set equal to a phone call, which is conservative

language_match_odds_ratio.source: WellSpan Health 2025, JMIR: language-matched outreach, adjusted odds ratio 2.01 for taking up screening

no_show_rate.source: Emirates Health Services primary care, Jul-Sep 2022: 14,038 no-shows of 67,429 booked appointments (JMIR Formative Research 2025)

text_opt_out_rate.source: Kaiser Permanente Colorado, JAMA Network Open 2021: 2.5% of adults opted out of automated health texts in a year

results_not_followed_up_low.source: Callen et al. 2011, J Gen Intern Med systematic review: abnormal lab results not followed up, lowest study

results_not_followed_up_high.source: Callen et al. 2011: abnormal lab results not followed up, highest study

capacity_per_day.source: New contacts per day, the same for both ways so the comparison is fair

reply_split.source: No published split of reply types; STOP is calibrated separately to the published opt-out rate

results_reply_split.source: No published value for replies to a nurse calling about a result

cannot_read_sms_factor.source: No published value for SMS replies from people who cannot read

barrier_reply_effect.source: No published value: replies fall by up to 40% with the highest access barrier

telehealth_boost.source: Primary care, 23 NYC public clinics, about 1.2 million visits (J Gen Intern Med 2022): telephone visits had adjusted odds ratio 0.82 for non-attendance against in-person in the later period; used as ln(1/0.82) on the attendance log-odds. Video visits did worse (odds ratio 2.02), so this applies to phone telehealth. Mobile clinics are given the same effect (assumption). Tested from 0 in the sensitivity analysis.

doctor_agree.source: A 2026 review found no study reporting doctors' agreement with AI decision support in primary care

prior_no_show_odds_ratio.source: Gebhart 2017, OHSU family medicine primary care: each earlier missed appointment, odds ratio 1.11 for a no-show (quality-improvement report, not peer reviewed)

lead_time_no_show_odds_ratio_per_day.source: Predictors of no-show in neurology clinics, Healthcare 2022: odds of a no-show rise 1.0019 times per day between booking and visit (a specialty clinic; no primary care per-day figure found)

reminder_no_show_reduction_automated.source: Hasvold and Wootton 2011, systematic review: automated reminders cut non-attendance by 29% of its usual level (against no reminder, so it may overstate an extra reminder)

reminder_no_show_reduction_call.source: Hasvold and Wootton 2011: a phone call by staff cut non-attendance by 39% of its usual level

transport_help_effect.source: Chaiyachati et al. 2018, JAMA Internal Medicine: offering free rides did not change missed primary care visits (36.5% vs 36.7%)

ramadan_attendance_effect.source: No study found that shows more missed visits in Ramadan; a trial in 36 Riyadh primary care centres recorded fewer no-shows during Ramadan, partly from recording errors. Set to no effect.

evening_slot_effect.source: No published effect of evening slots on attendance; set to no effect, so this system gets no credit for offering them

attendance_barrier_effect.source: Change in attendance log-odds from the lowest to the highest access barrier (language, insurance, day shift, phone, travel). No single published value for this combined score.

info_then_book.source: Share of people who book the day after asking for information. No published value found.

booking_lead_days.source: A visit is booked 2 to 10 days after the person says yes

prior_no_show_count_cap.source: Earlier missed visits count up to 3; beyond that the published odds ratio (measured on few repeat no-shows) is not extended

priority_weights.source: Priority score = weights x (risk, number of gaps out of 5, access barrier). Puts health need first and moves people with barriers up.

access_barrier_weights.source: Points for each barrier, adding up to at most 1; the travel part reaches its full weight at 90 minutes

no_reply_give_up_day.source: Days after the first message with no reply before the person is put back on the list

no_reply_retry_after_days.source: Days to wait before inviting someone again who never replied

on_hold_review_after_days.source: A card a doctor put on hold goes back to the doctor after a month

deadline_days.source: Days to make contact for each urgency level

risk_high_share.source: High risk = the top 15% of risk scores

risk_moderate_share.source: Moderate risk or above = the top 40% of risk scores

reminder_days.source: Days after the first message when this system sends a reminder on the same channel

followup_choice_days.source: Days after the first message when the follow-up chooser picks a reminder, a call or a health-worker visit

usual_care_reminder_day.source: Usual care: one reminder two weeks after the first message

telehealth_travel_min.source: After a missed visit, telehealth is offered when travel is over this many minutes (only for checks that can be done remotely)

later_pause_days.source: Pause after a LATER reply: a week when a result is waiting, a month otherwise

mobile_clinic_places.source: Each week a mobile clinic goes to this many rural or remote places with the most people waiting

noshow_model_min_auc.source: The no-show model plans support only if it ranks later visits at least this well

noshow_support_cutoffs.source: Fallback only (a model without its own cut-offs): predicted chance of missing at which support is added

support_rule.source: Used when the no-show model is not good enough: access barrier or past missed visits at which support is added

clinic_result_handling_day.source: Days after an abnormal result when the clinic's own result handling acts (at the published follow-up rate)

clinic_slots_per_day.source: Preventive-check appointments a day for these 5,000 people (clinic and telehealth share them); the same limit both ways. Busy days push bookings later.

mobile_clinic_slots.source: Visits one mobile clinic session can take; when full, people are booked at the clinic

mobile_clinic_first_day.source: Days after planning that the first mobile clinic of the week runs (one place a day after that)

priority_boosts.source: Added to the priority score: past the contact deadline, after a missed visit, after emergency words

max_rebooks.source: Rebookings after missed visits before the person rests and is invited again later

clinician_decides_checks.source: Checks a clinician must approve before anyone is contacted

telehealth_checks.source: Checks that can be done by a phone or video call; everything else needs a visit

noshow_support_shares.source: When the no-show model is used: an extra reminder for the 20% it ranks most likely to miss, a health-worker call for the top 5%

alerts.source: When the evaluation agent warns the team: people past their deadline, opt-outs today against last week, and the gap in reach between language groups; the same kind of alert is repeated within 7 days only if its number grows by half; opt-out spikes are compared with the last 7 days, fairness is checked every 7 days, and a repeated alert needs its number to grow by half

reach_floor_gap.source: Reach floor: a language, nationality, insurance or region group more than 10 points behind the best-reached group of its kind goes first within each urgency level, so giving priority to people with barriers never leaves another group far behind

run_date.source: The date every step treats as today (data adjustment, features, simulation start), so a rerun gives the same results. Override with PP_RUN_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD.

contact_windows.source: Best time to send: after iftar in Ramadan, Friday afternoon, after a day shift, otherwise late morning

max_message_characters.source: Longest message sent (two SMS segments); a longer template goes to a staff call

blocked_message_words.source: Words a message may never contain (privacy and no alarming language); such a message goes to a staff call

max_reply_probability.source: Upper limit on anyone's chance of replying in the simulation

uncalibrated_fallbacks.source: Used only before scripts/calibrate.py has run; the calibrated values replace them

age_groups.source: Age groups for fairness checks in the evaluation agent

fairness_age_bands.source: Age bands for the fairness tables in the results

outcome_window_days.source: Timely attendance and result follow-up are counted within 30 days

sensitivity.source: Settings tried in the worst-case analysis: 30% fewer replies, much lower attendance, doctors agreeing far less often, two random seeds; and a quarter fewer clinic slots (30 instead of 40 a day)

community_actions.source: When the Communities page suggests a school screening day, a mobile clinic or a health talk, and how small a place can be shown

map_min_people.source: Places with fewer people are not shown on the map (privacy)

phone_demo_people.source: People offered in the phone demo list

simulation.source: Length of the simulated period and its random seeds (same seeds, same results)

calibration.source: Usual care is calibrated over 6 runs (other seeds than the reported run) until attendance and opt-out are within these tolerances of the published figures

small_groups.source: Fairness tables hide groups under 10 people (privacy) and mark groups under 30 as not reliable

page_sizes.source: How many rows each page shows at first

urgent_slots.source: Appointments kept free each day for results reviews and other Urgent cases (as clinics keep same-week slots), booked 1 to 3 days ahead; the same rule in both ways

followup_actions.source: Follow-up options the learner chooses from, and the channel each one uses (none = the same channel)

value: Extra reminder the day before; offer a different time
Community health worker call before the visit; offer transport or telehealth
support_levels.source: Support added before a visit, from least to most

fairness_groups.source: Groups the evaluation agent checks for fair reach (the family's language decides the message, the person's own record the rest)

short_contact_day_weekday.source: Friday (Python weekday 4): UAE public-sector half day with Friday prayer, so the Friday contact window is used

weekly_review_every_days.source: Every 7 days the care-gap agent re-checks recalls and warning signs, and mobile clinic days are planned

streamlit_view.source: Display settings of the older Streamlit dashboard (map centred on Abu Dhabi emirate; list lengths)

gaps_for_full_score.source: The gaps part of the priority score reaches its full weight at 5 open care gaps

ai_features.source: Switch for the one AI step that acts inside the rules. learn_first_channel: the first message's channel is learned from replies, starting from the rule. It is off: over 5 seeds it did not improve completed care or the number of undiagnosed cases found (outputs/results/ai_ablation.json; python evaluate.py --ablation repeats it). Switch it on when a hospital's own data shows a gain

first_channel_learner.source: First-contact channel learner (Thompson sampling, like the follow-up learner). It chooses only among channels that need no staff time and that the person can use; everyone else keeps the rule's channel, and a person's own stated channel always wins. The rule's channel starts with this many assumed replies, so the learner departs from the rule only after real replies say so

spread_seeds.source: Random seeds for the seed-spread check (python evaluate.py --seeds): the headline results are re-run with each seed, both ways, and reported as the average and the range, so one run's luck is not mistaken for an effect
